messages.author: 3fcf0e009c95d23e
messages.subject: Using the Satterthwaite method
parts:
I have a couple of questions, but first a little background on my project:

I estimated densities of a species in seven strata (corresponding to
habitat types) using a global detection function and multiple covariates.
I also have two habitat types that were not sampled, but for my analysis I
will assume density in each of those unsampled strata is a function of
density in one of the 7 sampled strata. To estimate the total population
size (N), I am planning on summing the seven stratum-level population
estimates plus the theorized estimates from the two unsampled strata using
the delta method (as described in section 3.7.1). Afterwards I want to put
a confidence interval around N using the Satterthwaite adaptation described
in section 3.6.1 of the Introduction to Distance Sampling book.

Can anyone help me with these questions?

1. How do I obtain var(n) or cv(n)? I need one or the other to estimate
the df in equation 3.76, which in turn is used to calculate the constant
(the two-sided alpha-level t-distribution percentile) used in equation 3.73
to estimate confidence intervals. I see where the variance of sample size
is discussed in sections 3.6.2 and 5.4, but I would like to know if it can
be calculated in Distance rather than by hand. On page 79 there is this:
"The calculations may be carried out in Distance by setting sample effort
equal to ti for point i...". In my distance project I have set sampling
effort for points (it ranges from 4 to 1). When I run an analysis, on the
results page titled "Estimation Summary - Encounter rate" I see the value
of n for each stratum, but it has no cv. Likewise if I export the Stats
file for the analysis, the value of n is given but it has zero as the cv.
Have I set up my analysis incorrectly? Or should I calculate var(n) by
hand, or just assume var(n) = n?

2. To obtain the equivalent of equation 3.76 for point transect
sampling, do I just swap f(0) for h(0)?


If you are wondering why I don't just sit back and let Distance calculate
N-hat for me, there are two reasons. First, I want to include population
estimates for the unsampled strata, and second I plan to use not just
current land area in each stratum, but also projected land area at various
times in the future, allowing me to look for change over time.

Many thanks for your help,
Chris

var(x)=se(x)*se(x)
cv(x)=se(x)/x

where x is a parameter estimate. Described in first paragraph of 3.6.1

> >
> > 2. To obtain the equivalent of equation 3.76 for point transect
> > sampling, do I just swap f(0) for h(0)?

Yes. See bottom of page 69 where it says f(0) or h(0).
